messages.subject: Re: RApache while loop
parts:
Hi, Don:

The first thing to do is verify that your code works in an interactive R session.  If it doesn't work in an interactive R session, I would recommend posting to the R topic on stackexchange.com, where you can get general programming help.  If it does, then you should try writing the results of your code to stderr, so it ends up in the Apache log.  Something like this (untested):

  data <- tryCatch({
    rs <- dbSendQuery(con, paste("select * from test"))
    fetch(rs)
  },
  error=function(e) e)
  if (inherits(data, "error")) {
    cat(data, "\n", file=stderr())
  } else {
    # Format and return to the browser.
  }

Regards,

Nick



On Tue, Jun 10, 2014 at 8:47 AM, Dom Abbott <domab...@gmail.com> wrote:
Hi!

I've finally managed to get my RApache to talk to a DB! My next step is to be able to use the data retrieved to plot a graph.

My question is, how would I do a while loop in RApache?

The code in java would be something like this:

while ( rs.next() ) { 
String id = rs.getString("id"); 
}

I have tried that exact code (yes I'm optimistic) in RApache but that just throws an internal server error.

The code I'm using to retrieve the data is as follows:

rs = dbSendQuery(con, paste("select * from test"))
data = fetch(rs)

Any help would be greatly appreciated.

Thanks in advance!

parts:
Hi, Dom:

What I meant by interactive R session is just that R is usually used ... interactively.  Some people use an IDE [1]; others just run R from a terminal.  In both cases, though, the effect is the same: you type R code at a prompt, and the code is executed when you complete a statement (i.e. enter a complete line of code and press return.)  If you're just learning R, learning how to write the language in one of these interactive environments will take you a long way towards being able to know how to plot data.  

Regards,

Nick

[1] For example, http://www.rstudio.com/products/rstudio/download/
